name: IC-7300
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Icom publication and not affiliated with Icom.
verified: Compiled from the Icom IC-7300 Basic Manual and Icom's published specifications, September 2026. Not checked against a radio. Figures adjusted to the US model. Menu paths vary by firmware.
specs: 160 through 10 m, plus 6 m. US models have no 4 m band
13.8 V DC plus or minus 15 per cent
0.9 A standby, 1.25 A at full audio
USB Type-B, and a 3.5 mm remote jack. Both carry CI-V
keys: Opens the settings tree: set, keyer, decode and the rest.
Operating parameters for the current mode. A separate surface from MENU.
A short list of the things most often changed on whatever is showing. Faster than MENU.
Closes the screen and steps back a level.
Rotate to set the assigned function, push to pick items.
Swaps the VFOs. Hold to equalise them.
Cycles the memo pad. Hold to store what is displayed.
Tap toggles. Hold about a second to set the level.
Cycles the preamp. Hold about a second for the attenuator.
Tap toggles. Hold about a second for quick split.
Held, listens on the transmit frequency while split.
Hold about a second to reset the passband.
A brief touch beeps once. About a second gives the selection beep.
tasks: Press V/M. The display shows memory.
The up and down arrow keys.
Hold MPAD to capture the displayed frequency.
Set VFO A, press A/B, set VFO B, press SPLIT. Or hold SPLIT about a second for quick split.
Push MULTI, touch RF power, rotate. The scale is 0 to 100 per cent.
Partial reset clears the transceiver settings and leaves your memory channels alone.
All reset takes everything back to factory, memory channels included. Photograph them first.
control: The 3.5 mm remote jack on the rear, or over USB
Auto by default, following the connected controller
On by default, so the radio announces changes unasked
Not needed over USB. A CT-17 is only for the remote jack path
notes: Twenty-one amps at full output. Size the battery, the fuse and the wire for that, then run the power the contact needs.
It has a real internal tuner, which is the main thing separating it from the IC-7000 and IC-7100 in the field.
The waterfall is the reason people buy this radio and the reason they sit watching instead of calling.
Menu paths have moved between firmware revisions. If a path on this card is not on your radio, your firmware is the reason.
One antenna socket, HF and 6 m only. There is no VHF or UHF on this radio.
settings: CI-V address, as read from set mode
